extracted.intended_audience: Title IX Coordinators, LEA and IHE administrators, institutional compliance officers, and policy analysts implementing or assessing the Department's final Title IX regulations
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX final rule compliance guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory implementation and cost-impact guidance for recipients (LEAs, IHEs, and other recipients) describing required actions (training, supportive measures, investigations, recordkeeping, monitoring, appeals, informal resolution) and the Department's modeling assumptions for time and cost burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator training requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations increase training for Title IX Coordinators (the Department assumes trainings will be 2 hours longer for each Title IX Coordinator in Year 1, and 1 hour longer in future years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department estimates training costs of $4,774,191 in Year 1 and $2,387,096 in each succeeding year. Costs will also be incurred to update training materials; the Department assumes a one-time training development cost for Title IX Coordinators equal to $9,548,382. Materials may be developed in various ways (some entities may develop materials used across many recipients). The Department did not receive supplementary data to revise these estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to offer supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer supportive measures, as appropriate, to complainants and respondents in response to information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, including sex-based harassment and prohibited retaliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expands beyond the 2020 amendments (which required offering supportive measures only in response to actual knowledge of sexual harassment). Supportive measures may be varied and tailored; examples include academic adjustments (e.g., allowing a student to attend a different section) and counseling. The Department added a flat cost of $250 per incident to account for potential costs and used common supportive measures when estimating costs. The Department cannot specify every supportive measure due to variability across recipients and cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures: per-incident time and cost assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Per-incident staff time and flat-cost assumptions used to estimate burden of providing supportive measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At LEAs: 2 hours from a Title IX Coordinator and 2 hours from an administrative assistant plus $250 flat = approx. $565 per incident (using $61.14/hour for admin). At IHEs and other recipients: 2 hours from a Title IX Coordinator and 1 hour from an administrative assistant plus $250 flat = approx. $504 per incident. The Department assumes supportive measures are accepted in ~90% of incidents in which offered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of supportive measures for non-harassment sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: For allegations of sex discrimination other than sex-based harassment or prohibited retaliation, recipients are not required to alter the conduct alleged to be sex discrimination for the purpose of providing a supportive measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department expects little impact on costs for these situations because many instances (e.g., unequal facilities) have few appropriate supportive measures beyond eliminating the source of discrimination; educational-settings discrimination often yields academic supportive measures with relatively minor costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling assumptions about change in supportive-measure incidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department assumes the number of incidents prompting an offer of supportive measures will increase approximately 100% under the final regulations versus the number of investigations conducted under the 2020 amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This doubling reflects broader scope and increased clarity; the Department assumes recipients will offer supportive measures more often and that acceptance rates are ~90%. Estimated mean provisions per year after final regulations: each LEA 6.40, each IHE 11.29, other recipients 3.96. Net annual increase in provision costs estimated at $9,142,455.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX jurisdictional scope (geographic applicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.11 clarifies Title IX applies to every recipient and all prohibited sex discrimination occurring under a recipient's education program or activity in the United States, even when some contributing conduct occurred outside the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are not obligated under Title IX to receive/process complaints or commence grievance procedures about conduct occurring outside the US unless that conduct is alleged to have contributed to a sex-based hostile environment under the recipient's education program or activity in the United States. Investigations of conduct that occurred outside the US but contributed domestically may be more time-consuming; such investigations are discretionary when outside the final regulations' requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient response typology (Groups A, B, C) and exercise of flexibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department categorizes recipients into three groups to model likely responses: Group A (will see increases in investigations but will exercise flexibilities reducing per-complaint burden), Group B (will see increases and maintain structures similar to 2020 amendments, including alternative processes), Group C (little or no change).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department assumes exercising flexibilities will not impact ability to ensure fair investigations/adjudications but will allow tailored, less burdensome procedures. Modeling and cost estimates are provided separately for each group and recipient type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation and adjudication time-burden estimates (Group A baseline and after-final)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assumed hours per role for investigations/adjudications for Group A recipients under baseline (2020 amendments) and after final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baseline (Group A): LEAs — Title IX Coordinator 3h, Adm. Assistant 4h, 2 lawyers/advisors 2h each (involved ~15% cases), Investigator 6h, Adjudicator 2h. IHEs — Title IX Coordinator 6h, Adm. Assistant 8h, 2 lawyers/advisors 5h each (15% cases), Investigator 10h, Adjudicator 2h. After final regs (Group A): LEAs — Title IX Coordinator 4h, Adm. Assistant 2h; IHEs — Title IX Coordinator 5h, Adm. Assistant 8h, 2 lawyers/advisors 5h each, Investigator 10h, Adjudicator 2h. Department estimates net burden increase for Group A investigations/adjudications to $9,747,693 per year (a $3,001,009 increase). A flat recording cost of $100 per adjudication is assumed where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording/transcript requirements for IHEs and meeting records
rubrics_metrics.description: IHEs are required to create an audio or audiovisual recording, or transcript, of all live hearings; §106.46(f)(1)(i)(C) requires a postsecondary institution to create a recording or transcript of individual meetings with a party or witness conducted to satisfy §106.46(f)(1)(i)(A), even if no live hearing is held.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the final regulations, IHEs may but are not required to hold live hearings; when recordings/transcripts are required, the Department assumes a flat recording cost (modeled at $100 per investigation in many cases and $200 in some IHE contexts to account for transcripts). LEAs and many other recipients are assumed to have no or minimal recording costs because they are not required to hold live hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lawyer/advisor involvement assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Modeling assumptions about when lawyers/advisors are involved in investigations and appeals and how many are present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department assumes two lawyers/advisors when present. For Group A modeling, lawyers/advisors are involved in approximately 15% of investigations/adjudications. Other models assume 5% involvement for certain alternative processes. These percentages drive estimated time and cost impacts for lawyer/advisor hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative disciplinary process assumptions (Group B)
rubrics_metrics.description: For many recipients in Group B, incidents outside the §106.45 grievance process were shifted into alternative disciplinary processes; the Department models these processes as mirroring recipient student conduct processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LEA alternative process assumptions: administrator 3h ($96.46/hr), administrative assistant 14h, lawyers/advisors 6h each in 5% of cases, investigator 6h; adjudication split assumptions (75% administered by admin who doubles burden, 25% by independent adjudicator 2h). IHE: administrator 6h, administrative assistant 20h, 2 lawyers/advisors 10h each, investigator 15h; adjudication split (60% admin adjudicator doubling, 40% independent adjudicator 8h). For other recipients: administrator 4h, administrative assistant 8h. Under final regulations, many of these incidents will instead be handled under Title IX grievance procedures and the Department provides revised hour estimates per role for Group B after final regs. The Department estimates net decreases/increases in burden accordingly (e.g., Group B net decrease around $63,650,843).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording cost assumptions per hearing/investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Modeling uses flat recording/transcript cost assumptions per hearing or investigation depending on recipient type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common modeled values: $100 per hearing/investigation for LEAs and many other recipients; IHEs sometimes modeled at $200 per hearing to account for transcripts or more extensive records. For Group A the Department assumed $100 per adjudication for recording; for Group B the Department assumed $200 for some IHE hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal process requirements and parity
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations require all recipients to offer an appeal of a dismissal of a sex discrimination complaint; IHEs must continue to offer an appeal process for sex-based harassment complaints involving a student party. Appeals offered must, at minimum, be the same as appeals in other comparable proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department assumes ~50% of fully adjudicated complaints have at least one party appeal (consistent with 2020 estimates). Time assumptions per appeal: LEA — 2h Title IX Coordinator, 2h Adm. Assistant, 2 lawyers/advisors 2h each, 6h adjudicator; IHE — 2h Title IX Coordinator, 4h Adm. Assistant, 2 lawyers/advisors 5h each, 8h adjudicator; Other recipients similar to IHE adjudicator 8h. The Department estimates additional annual cost from increased appeals of approximately $17,776,304.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution: expected burden and changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the final regulations, the Department expects de minimis change in the proportion of complaints resolved via informal resolution and no significant change in per-instance burden; however, informal resolution is modeled as requiring more Title IX Coordinator and administrative assistant time than investigative processes while eliminating other costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumed additional burdens for informal resolution over investigation: LEA +1h Title IX Coordinator and +5h administrative assistant; IHE +2.5h Title IX Coordinator and +1h administrative assistant; other recipients +1h Title IX Coordinator and +3h administrative assistant. Informal resolution assumed to remove burdens for investigators, adjudicators, recording at all levels and eliminate lawyers/advisors costs at LEA and other recipients; IHE informal resolution still modeled with 6h each for two lawyers/advisors. Estimated increase in informal resolution costs due to higher complaint volume ~ $14,068,164 per year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping expansion under final §106.8(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.8(f) broadens recordkeeping requirements to apply to all notifications to the Title IX Coordinator about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination and all complaints of sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some recipients already maintain such records; others that previously preserved only sexual-harassment records will face increased burdens. Modeled Year 1 modification costs: LEA — 2h Title IX Coordinator + 2h administrative assistant; IHE — 4h Title IX Coordinator + 8h administrative assistant + 4h database administrator ($77.54/hr); other recipients — 2h Title IX Coordinator + 2h administrative assistant. Total Year 1 modification estimate ~$13,022,034. Ongoing annual increases modeled: LEA +1h each Title IX Coordinator/admin assistant; IHE +1h Title IX Coordinator +5h administrative assistant; other recipients +1h each; ongoing annual cost ~$5,237,728.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring for barriers to reporting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must ensure their Title IX Coordinator monitors the education program or activity for barriers to reporting information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination and take steps reasonably calculated to address such barriers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many recipients (particularly IHEs) already monitor for barriers. Options to monitor with de minimis cost include incorporating barrier-related questions into existing training materials, adding such questions to conversations with stakeholders, roundtable discussions, listening sessions, or other low-cost mechanisms. The Department assumes Title IX Coordinators are motivated to proactively identify and address sex discrimination and that many will select low-cost monitoring options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling assumptions about investigation frequency and per-recipient counts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department models the number of investigations/provisions/appeals per recipient per year to estimate aggregate costs under baseline and final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of modeled frequencies: pre-2020 average investigations per year — LEAs 3.23 (baseline used elsewhere 1.94 depending on group), IHEs and others vary by group and baseline; after-final modeled averages include LEAs providing supportive measures 6.40 times/year and conducting 3.55–3.82 investigations/year depending on group, IHEs conducting 6.27 investigations/year (Group A/B after-final values differ by table). These frequency assumptions feed cost estimates; commenters did not provide sufficient data to alter these modeled frequencies.
